option_relations.rationale: Bacterial myositis is a broader category that includes intramuscular abscesses, which is the specific diagnosis in the vignette.

Deep neck space infection refers to infections in specific fascial planes of the neck, whereas the vignette describes an intramuscular abscess within the levator scapulae muscle, which is not typically classified as a deep neck space infection.

Pyomyositis of the levator scapulae muscle caused by Fusobacterium necrophorum is clinically equivalent to an intramuscular abscess of the left levator scapulae muscle, as pyomyositis often presents as an abscess and the pathogen is specified in the vignette.

Cervical intramuscular abscess (levator scapulae) due to F. necrophorum is clinically equivalent to an intramuscular abscess of the left levator scapulae muscle, providing the specific location and pathogen as described in the vignette.
